subject: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ check — asks and draft KPIs
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ check — asks and draft KPIs

Team —

We're lining up the QBR pack for next week and I want to lock the infra capacity / unit-econ section today so leadership has clean ask slides. Key context: product usage has a higher peak density over the last 60 days (noted on the dashboard) and we need a succinct set of scenarios (baseline, +20% surge, +60% holiday surge) with clear levers and expected $/token and per-VM GPU run-rates.

Attached: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (runway scenarios + pivot tables) and kpi_snapshot_20261013.pdf

Immediate asks:
- Can engineering (Karthik) confirm the assumptions I flagged in the model: current avg GPU utilization (42%), slot overcommit headroom (15%), and KV-cache hit rate baseline (12%)? If those numbers look off, call out where.
- Leadership (Lauren): I'd like a single-slide ask (reserve vs burst vs pricing) that we can present; what tolerance do you want on the numbers? Do we show best-effort ranges or single-point asks?
- Ops (Marissa): procurement implications — if we propose a reserved + burst mix (described in sheet "Hybrid Runway"), can you run the procurement lead-time for reserved capacity changes and a high-level estimate for credits?

Quick summary of my baseline numbers in the sheet (so you don't have to open it right away):
- Monthly GPU spend (hosted + dedicated blended): $1,170,000
- Avg GPU utilization: 42%
- Effective per-token spend (hosted inference + infra amortized): $0.00078/token (million token bucket)
- Potential savings with 3 levers (batching+, KV cache, quantization): 12–28% depending on scenario

Timebox: please respond with confirmations or redlines by EOD (PST) so I can fold into the leadership deck.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: qbr_capacity_model_v3.xlsx (xlsx), kpi_snapshot_20261013.pdf (pdf)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ check — asks and draft KPIs

Connor —

Thanks for the model. Quick confirmations + a few technical clarifications after looking at "Hybrid Runway":

Confirmed numbers (today, measured over last 30d production telemetry):
- Avg GPU utilization: 41.8% (rounded to 42% in the sheet) — this is measured across the dedicated fleet only, hosted mixes add ~3pp variance by region
- Slot overcommit headroom: 14% (safely 15% in slides)
- KV-cache baseline (prefix + long-lived session reuse): 11.5% (12% is fine)

Assumptions I changed in the model (I annotated the sheet):
- Batching latency SLO: assumed no more than +25ms p50 with 2x batching for typical gen workloads. If leadership won't accept p50 increase, effective batching multiplier reduces (and so do savings).
- Quantization profile: we can push stable 4-bit for some families; savings estimate in model assumes 18% runtime speedup for 4-bit on Ampere-like hardware with no accuracy regression. If we require 8-bit-only, swap ~8% speedup.

Short scenario math (rounded):
- Baseline monthly spend: $1.17M
- Baseline effective unit cost: $0.00078/token
- +20% steady load (no levers): $1.40M/month (utilization improves to ~52%)
- +20% with recommended levers (moderate batching 1.6x, cache hit -> 24%): $1.20M/month (~8.5% savings vs naive surge)
- +60% holiday surge (aggressive burst): naive: $1.87M; hybrid (reserve 40% base, burst transient): $1.45M — key is the mix and time-windowing of burst.

Operational impacts to call out in the QBR slide:
- Tail latency risk with batching: we must show SLO margin and fallback policy (route to faster instance type or smaller batch path).
- Cache warmup behavior: when we route to new slots, initial requests will be cache cold — estimate 6–12h to warm for long-lived convo patterns. Show cache hit ramp in the slide.

I've added two small charts in the workbook: util vs cost curve and a heatmap of batch multiplier vs p50 delta.

If you want, I can prepare a 1-slide "what we need from leadership" with the exact reserve vs burst numbers and the expected procurement ask.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
VP, Serving & Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ check — asks and draft KPIs

Connor — thanks for the concise summary. A couple of editorial asks from leadership side before we finalize the slide:

1) Present numbers as ranges with clear ask point. Example: "We request $X reserved to cover baseline (+20% headroom) — shown as P50 estimate; downside P75 and upside P25 numbers are noted." Leadership prefers to see the ask and a conservative scenario.
2) On the savings %: show the low/likely/high bands (e.g., batching low 3% / likely 10% / high 18%) rather than a single 12–28% span — the table is easier to digest with three buckets.
3) We need the procurement lead-time expressed in business days (not just weeks) because finance asks for exact cutoff dates for commit changes.

Please make the 1-slide ask that Karthik offered (call it "Reserve + Burst ask: what we need from leadership") and include:
- Reserve capacity (vGPU equivalence) and dollar ask
- Expected latency/regression risk with each lever and fallback policy
- Procurement cutoff date for Q4 commit changes (marissa)

I'm comfortable with showing single-point P50 for the ask and ranges for sensitivity. If you can get procurement numbers by 4pm PST I'll slot the slide into the deck.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Product
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Hannah TechOps <hannah.ops@acmeai.com>, Procurement <procure@acmeai.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: QBR runway: capacity & unit-econ check — asks and draft KPIs

Forwarding procurement/ops info — Connor/Team, looping in Acme folks for lead-time and credit checks. Below is my operational read and the procurement questions (short):

Operational read (short):
- If leadership approves the hybrid reserve+burst ask at P50: we need a 30–45 business-day lead time to secure new reserved pools that match the performance SKU. That includes contract sign-off and regional provisioning.
- For burst capacity (spot or transient), lead time is effectively immediate but has availability and price variability; recommend we keep a 15% safety margin on burst sizing.
- If we move more aggressively on quantization and batching, the provisioning footprint can shift (e.g., more CPU on host, less GPU hours) — that creates a small ops rework but no extra lead time.

Procurement questions for Acme:
1) What is the earliest commit date we can change for Q4 to get reserved capacity live by Nov 15, 2026? Please confirm in business days.
2) Are there bulk-credit discounts or early-commit credits we should model for a 12-month reserved contract vs monthly on-demand?
3) Any SOW or security checklist we should route now so provisioning is not delayed?

Acme — if you can respond with (1) business-day lead time for reserved capacity to be live by Nov 15 and (2) whether bulk credits apply for 12-month commitment, that'd be great.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Platform Ops — Supply & Procurement
Redwood Inference
